Where to catch what

Tap or click an area on the map, pick one below, or search for a Pokemon. 61 land areas, 3 sea bands, 1 creek and 66 route-path sections; 607 species.

  • Coloured areas are the campaign's encounter areas, one per Nuzlocke catch zone. Thin white lines are their drawn borders; the colour shows exactly where the table applies. Striped bands are route paths, which carry their own table; the dashed line is the route's centre.
  • Blue on the relief is water: ground below sea level (y62). Dots are towns.
  • Buckets. Every spawn first rolls a bucket, then a Pokemon inside it. The server's weights are common 94, uncommon 5, rare 0.5, ultra-rare 0.2 (per 100 rolls). Day and Night are the chance that one spawn at that kind of spot (land, water surface, underwater, floor) is that Pokemon. Hover a bucket badge for the share inside the bucket. A range (e.g. 3.1%-4.0%) means the chance differs across the area.
  • Those chances are an estimate: they assume the bucket roll only counts buckets the spot has (not confirmed for Cobblemon 1.8), treat height and nearby-water conditions as met, and leave rain-only Pokemon out of the sum (they show "in rain"). Land and surface spawns need open sky: nothing on these tables spawns under a roof or in a cave.
  • No campaign spawn is limited by biome: the area is the condition. Conditions that do apply are written under the Pokemon's name.

What this map does not show

  • It is not everything. Outside the campaign's areas the modpack's own default spawns still run (by design: off-route wilderness; optional islands; open ocean outside authored sites and marine zones; unauthored caves; Nether; End; postgame unless later progression policy changes it). Inside them the defaults are meant to be switched off. Fishing is not covered.
  • Discoveries are left for you to find: legendary and mythical Pokemon, resident Pokemon, the Mega dens and their families, shrines, caches, portals, and story encounters.
  • Rarer spots inside areas (65 areas have one, with stronger alpha Pokemon) are not marked.
  • Nests in old trees and saplings carry their own birds (67 nest tables). Professor Oak knows more.
  • Victory Road's caves (11 cave tables) are part of the final climb and not listed; its outdoor path is.
  • Other special places with their own tables (17, plus 8 training grounds not yet built) are not shown.
  • Held items on wild Pokemon are not listed.
  • This page is generated from the campaign's data. The server may run an older or newer copy; what you meet in game wins.

Data notes

Where the data and a design document (or two data files) disagree. The compiled data is what the game reads, so the page follows it.

  • Bucket weights: docs/mechanics/ENCOUNTER_DESIGN.md gives common 88.5, uncommon 10, rare 1.2, ultra-rare 0.3 (Cobbleverse's 1.7 config). The server's recorded config (server/config/mods/cobblemon/spawning/best-spawner-config.json worldBuckets) says common 94, uncommon 5, rare 0.5, ultra-rare 0.2. This page uses the server's.
  • data/regions.json still marks 61 sub-regions' encounters as "empty, not populated" (e.g. arrow_creeks, arrow_lake_shores, crater_rim_north_west); their compiled pools are populated, and the compiled pools are what the game reads.
  • The Wooper creek: data/nuzlocke_zones.json gives levels 24-35, the compiled pool (its rarer spot excluded) 24-30.
  • jungle_east: compiled with 14 land Pokemon, but none of its 18 boxes has ground at or above sea level (y62) on the heightmap (4-block downsample), so nothing in it can spawn; left off the map. data/nuzlocke_zones.json lists it under not_zones too.
  • jungle_west: compiled with 20 land Pokemon, but none of its 20 boxes has ground at or above sea level (y62) on the heightmap (4-block downsample), so nothing in it can spawn; left off the map. data/nuzlocke_zones.json lists it under not_zones too.
